title: Interleaved CUDA-graph checkpointing and rollback for multi-stream decode
creator: Sasha Patel
description:
Problem: In multi-stream decode we intermittently see CUDA Graph capture failures and nondeterministic replay behavior when streams interleave prefill and decode. Failures manifest as corrupted KV cache pointers, transient hangs on recapture, or incorrect token outputs after a fallback. Root causes are a combination of: 1) capture timing windows where prefill and decode kernels race, 2) stream-affinity assumptions baked into captured kernels, and 3) lack of a safe checkpoint/rollback mechanism for partial captures.

Goal: Implement a lightweight checkpointing and rollback mechanism that makes CUDA Graph capture and replay idempotent across interleaved streams and prefill/decode transitions. The feature should: (a) detect unsafe capture windows and defer/retry captures deterministically, (b) provide a compact snapshot (checkpoint) of KV-cache pointers + stream-state to allow rollback on recapture, and (c) expose a safe synchronous fallback path when recapture fails after N retries.

Non-goals: Full transactional KV-store implementation, or major changes to kernel logic. This ticket focuses on orchestration and small runtime metadata changes to make captures robust with minimal perf impact.
acceptance_criteria: Deterministic capture success rate >= 99.9% on the multi-stream stress harness (50 concurrent streams, variable seq-lens 8-2048)
On recapture failure, runtime can rollback to pre-capture checkpoint and continue decoding with synchronous fallback within 50ms median additional latency
No output-regression on the standard eval prompt set (per-token match >= 99.995%)
Implement unit + integration tests covering checkpoint creation, rollback, and fallback, with CI job added to runtime-stability pipeline
test_plan: Add unit tests for checkpoint metadata creation and restore (mocked stream and KV pointers)
Extend multi-stream stress harness to assert capture idempotency across 10k capture/replay cycles
Run comparative latency/throughput benchmarks (baseline vs checkpointing) on p4d and a40 instances; report p50/p95/p99 token latency and tokens/sec
Create a canary on Dedicated to run capture-heavy traffic for 48h and monitor graph recapture rate and error alarms
updates: 2026-02-20 - Created: scoped problem, initial design options (snapshot, tombstone, deferred-capture). Assigned to Marco Li.
2026-02-25 - Spike completed: microbench of snapshot size showed 128-256 bytes per stream for minimal metadata (stream-id, kv-gen, seq-offset, graph-version). Memory overhead < 3% for 512 streams.

2026-03-01 - Design decision: use compact checkpoint (metadata-only) plus a recapture token to make recapture idempotent. Chose deterministic retry backoff (fixed 3 retries, 20ms backoff) rather than exponential to bound latency.

2026-03-03 - Implementation: added checkpoint create/restore hooks in graph-capture path. Instrumented tracepoints for 'checkpoint_created' and 'checkpoint_restored'. Initial PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4762

2026-03-05 - Benchmark: capture success rose from 98.1% -> 99.7% on stress harness. p95 extra latency for successful capture ~ +6ms. Noted pathological case when KV-gen wraps quickly for tiny sequences; added wrap handling in checkpoint metadata.

2026-03-07 - Code review feedback from K. Nguyen: make recapture token include per-kernel fingerprint and add feature-flag gating for canary rollout. Addressed in PR feedback, pushed update. PR link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4762/files#diff

2026-03-10 - Integration tests added. CI: runtime-stability job passes locally. Planning Dedicated canary for 2026-03-12. Observability: dashboard created for checkpoint metrics: grafana/dashboard?id=cdg-checkpointing
notes: Tradeoffs considered: snapshotting full KV tensors would be robust but memory- and time-expensive; metadata-only checkpoints reduce memory but require careful validation at restore.
Fallback behavior: after 3 recapture retries, fallback to synchronous decode on the same stream. This keeps correctness and avoids blocking other streams but increases tail latency for that request.
We intentionally avoid adding heavyweight locks around capture; prefer optimistic capture + rollback to preserve throughput.
Related incident: postmortem from ENG-28350 highlighted recurrent recapture ordering bug that this work addresses indirectly.
implementation_notes: Checkpoint layout: <u64 stream_tag> | <u32 kv_gen> | <u32 seq_offset> | <u32 kernel_fingerprint> | <u8 flags>
Recapture token: uses (stream_tag, checkpoint_hash, kernel_fingerprint) to ensure idempotent recapture even if physical memory addresses shifted
API changes: capture API adds optional 'checkpoint_handle' out-param that runtime uses internally. No surface API change for customers.
Metrics: checkpoint_created, checkpoint_restored, recapture_attempts, recapture_failures, fallback_sync_count
Perf mitigation: checkpoint allocation uses preallocated pool to avoid malloc in hot path; pool size tunable per-device
linked_prs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4791 (follow-up to add feature flag and telemetry)
qa_notes: When validating on canary, monitor 'fallback_sync_count' — any nonzero steady rate indicates remaining instability and should block broad rollout.
Run output-regression harness from evals/ci against canary traffic snapshot to detect subtle mismatches due to race windows.
If we observe >0.01% token mismatches, revert feature-flag and open hotfix (ENG-hotfix-capture)
